intent: I increased the wheel track from 0.17 to 0.18 to further enhance lateral stability during turns, as the integrator feedback suggested this would help reduce off-track events. I moved the two rear sensors further back from y = -0.02 to y = -0.03 to enable even earlier detection of sharp turns, giving the controller more time to react and reduce line loss events. I kept the sensor size at 0.016, the maximum allowed, to maintain noise robustness. These changes aim to provide the controller with better early line information and a more stable platform, improving completion rates and progress while reducing line loss events and off-track terminations.
rationale: The previous iteration moved rear sensors to y = -0.02 and increased wheel track to 0.17, which improved stability and early turn detection but the robot still failed to complete tracks with one line loss event per run and off-track termination around 60% progress. The integrator feedback recommended further increasing wheel track to 0.18 and moving rear sensors further back to y = -0.03 to detect turns earlier. Moving sensors further back should allow the controller to anticipate turns sooner, reducing line loss events. Increasing wheel track enhances lateral stability, helping maintain control during turns and reducing off-track failures. Sensor size remains at 0.016 to keep noise robustness high. I expect these geometry changes to reduce line loss events, improve progress and completion rates, and provide a more stable and responsive platform for the controller to exploit.
